criteria.descriptor: All technical claims are correct: LDA as a bag-of-words model, short-text sparsity, perplexity not tracking interpretability, coherence metrics (NPMI/c_v), and the proposed pipeline's components (embeddings, UMAP, HDBSCAN's density-based/outlier behaviour, c-TF-IDF). No fabricated mechanisms (e.g., claiming BERTopic needs k up front, or that perplexity measures coherence). Full marks require accurate mechanisms, not just correct tool names.

Covers all five asks: LDA/perplexity diagnosis, a concrete alternative pipeline, its trade-offs, the streaming/evolving-topics handling, and an evaluation plan. Full marks address every part substantively; partial credit if the streaming aspect or the honest trade-offs are missing or only gestured at.

Choices are justified by linking each fix to a specific failure (embeddings -> synonymy/short text; HDBSCAN -> no k and outliers; coherence -> interpretability) and the answer weighs costs rather than presenting BERTopic as strictly superior. Full marks show cause-and-effect reasoning and genuine trade-off analysis.

Reads as a clear, well-organised design-review response that a mixed technical/stakeholder audience could follow, with correct terminology used precisely. Full marks for logical structure across the five parts and unambiguous phrasing.

expected_answer_points: Diagnoses LDA's core weaknesses for this data: bag-of-words ignores semantics/synonymy (so 'refund'/'chargeback' don't group), and very short tickets cause document-term sparsity that makes per-document topic mixtures poorly estimated; k must also be fixed a priori.

Identifies that selecting k by perplexity is itself an error - perplexity measures predictive fit, not interpretability, and does not correlate (can anti-correlate) with human topic quality; coherence (NPMI/c_v), diversity, and human inspection are the right signals.

Proposes a concrete embedding-based pipeline (e.g., BERTopic: sentence-transformer embeddings -> UMAP -> HDBSCAN -> c-TF-IDF), or a short-text model (GSDMM/biterm), and explains that embeddings capture semantic similarity so paraphrases cluster and short text is handled.
Notes that HDBSCAN is density-based - it discovers the number of clusters automatically and marks outliers - rather than forcing a pre-specified k like LDA/k-means.

Is honest about trade-offs: heavier compute/GPU, potentially large outlier (-1) cluster and how to mitigate it, hard single-topic assignment (loses genuinely multi-topic tickets), and reduced statistical/explanatory transparency.
Addresses the streaming/evolving-topics requirement: periodic re-fit vs transform-only, online/incremental variants, dynamic topics-over-time, topic merging/guided seeding, and monitoring drift.

Specifies an evaluation plan using multiple signals (coherence, diversity, outlier proportion, stability) plus human or downstream validation, treating automatic metrics as necessary but not sufficient.
common_pitfalls: Blames only preprocessing (stopwords, lemmatisation) or 'not enough data' and never confronts the fundamental bag-of-words + short-text-sparsity limitation, so the fix stays within LDA when the modelling approach itself is the problem.

Treats perplexity or held-out log-likelihood as a valid topic-quality metric and merely suggests re-tuning k, unaware that coherence (NPMI/c_v) is the interpretability signal and perplexity can anti-correlate with it.

Recommends BERTopic as strictly better while ignoring its costs - embedding/GPU compute, a potentially huge -1 outlier cluster, and hard single-topic assignment that cannot represent a ticket spanning two themes.

Confuses the clustering step: claims BERTopic still needs the number of topics specified up front, or conflates HDBSCAN (density-based, discovers k, produces outliers) with k-means (needs k, assigns everything).
Hand-waves the streaming requirement with 'just retrain nightly' and does not address topic alignment/drift across re-fits, incremental/online options, or dynamic topics-over-time.
Proposes only a single automatic metric (or none) for evaluation and omits human inspection or a downstream validation, so topic quality is never grounded in interpretability.
reference_answer:
The prior attempt failed for two largely independent reasons: the model is a poor fit for this data, and the selection metric was the wrong signal.

Why LDA struggled. LDA is a bag-of-words generative model that infers per-document topic mixtures and per-topic word distributions purely from word co-occurrence (with Dirichlet priors). Two properties hurt here. First, it has no notion of semantics: 'refund', 'money back' and 'chargeback' are distinct tokens, so paraphrases only group if they literally co-occur, which explains why synonyms scattered across topics. Second, support tickets are very short, so each document contributes only a handful of co-occurring words; the per-document topic distribution is estimated from almost no evidence. That short-text sparsity produces diffuse, overlapping topics. LDA also forces k to be fixed up front.

Why k=20-by-perplexity was wrong. Perplexity (held-out likelihood) measures predictive fit, not interpretability, and is well known not to correlate - sometimes to anti-correlate - with human-judged topic quality (Chang et al., 'Reading Tea Leaves'). The right signals are topic coherence (NPMI or c_v), topic diversity, and human inspection. If the team kept LDA, they should sweep k and select by coherence, not perplexity, and tighten preprocessing (stopwords, lemmatisation, filter_extremes, n-grams).

A better pipeline. I would move to an embedding-based approach such as BERTopic: encode each ticket with a sentence-transformer, reduce dimensionality with UMAP, cluster with HDBSCAN, then derive topic keywords with class-based TF-IDF (c-TF-IDF), optionally refining labels with MMR/KeyBERT or an LLM. Embeddings capture semantic similarity, so paraphrases cluster even without shared tokens - directly fixing both weaknesses on short text. HDBSCAN is density-based: it discovers the number of clusters and labels genuine noise as outliers instead of forcing every ticket into a topic. A short-text-specific alternative is GSDMM or a biterm topic model, which assume one topic per short document.

Trade-offs to flag. BERTopic is heavier (embedding compute, ideally a GPU); HDBSCAN can dump a large share of tickets into the -1 outlier cluster (mitigate by tuning min_cluster_size, using reduce_outliers, or swapping in k-means if full assignment is required); and assignment is hard/single-topic, so unlike LDA it will not model a ticket that genuinely spans two themes. It is also less statistically principled and its clusters are harder to explain to stakeholders.

Streaming and evolving topics. New themes appear over time, so a single static fit degrades. I would fit once and transform incoming tickets for day-to-day stability, but periodically re-fit to capture new topics; use BERTopic's online mode (IncrementalPCA + MiniBatchKMeans + OnlineCountVectorizer) for true incremental updates; use dynamic topic modelling (topics-over-time) to track how known topics evolve; and use merge_topics/reduce_topics plus guided seeding for categories the business already cares about. Monitor the outlier rate and coherence over time as a drift signal.

Evaluation. Report coherence (NPMI), topic diversity, outlier proportion and run-to-run stability, but treat automatic metrics as necessary-not-sufficient: confirm with human review or a downstream proxy such as ticket-routing accuracy.
